businessModel: Business model type relevant to test scenario
sourceNote: Synthetic case created to stress-test diagnosis engine on specific failure mode archetype. All data generated to be realistic and representative. No cases replicate Round 1 synthetic patterns. No answer-key content embedded in case inputs.

ownerIntake.businessType: Realistic business description matching the stress-test scenario (e.g., 'B2B SaaS platform for supply chain optimization, serving mid-market manufacturers')
ownerIntake.stage: Stage with metrics designed to trigger the target failure mode (e.g., for UNIT_ECONOMICS_BREAKDOWN test: 'Post-Series B, $8M ARR growing 35% YoY, but unit economics deteriorating: CAC $45k, LTV $120k (3-year payback)')
ownerIntake.ownerGoal: Goal that makes the stress-test scenario salient (e.g., 'Prepare for Series C fundraising within 12 months while demonstrating unit economics improvement')
ownerConstraints: Constraint that intensifies the stress-test scenario (e.g., 'Cannot raise additional capital until unit economics improve' or 'Board requires profitability path within 2 years')
Structural constraint supporting the test (e.g., 'Sales cycles 6-9 months, so early customer cohort LTV data sparse')
Resource constraint relevant to remediation (e.g., 'Engineering team fully allocated to product; no capacity for experimental optimizations')
ownerIntake.immediateConcern: The specific problem the scenario poses (e.g., 'With current unit economics, scaling to $100M ARR will require $300M+ in cumulative CapEx, but capital is constrained. What drives unit economics deterioration?')
availableData: Financial metrics: ARR, MRR, gross margin %, customer acquisition cost (CAC), customer lifetime value (LTV), payback period
Operational data: Sales cycle length, time to first dollar, customer retention cohorts, expansion revenue per customer, churn by cohort age
Customer data: Customer acquisition channels, pricing tiers, customer size distribution, satisfaction scores
unavailableData: Specific competitor pricing or win/loss data
Detailed product usage analytics (assumed available internally but not disclosed)
Market research on willingness to pay or price elasticity
ownerIntake.timeHorizon: 180 days (6-month decision point: Series C prep or strategic pivot)
ownerIntake.riskAppetite: MEDIUM (funding-dependent company must balance growth with economics)

clientContext.revenueImpactUrgency: HIGH (unit economics directly impact fundraising ability and long-term viability)

businessProblem: Synthetic scenario statement: 'A B2B SaaS company with strong revenue growth (35% YoY, $8M ARR) faces deteriorating unit economics as it scales. CAC has risen 40% from $32k to $45k due to market saturation in initial segment, while LTV has declined 15% from $142k to $120k due to earlier-cohort churn acceleration. The company must diagnose whether the deterioration is systemic (product-market fit erosion) or resolvable (pricing, sales efficiency, or retention-specific intervention). Series C timing depends on the diagnosis.'

evidence.finding: Unit economics deterioration (e.g., 'LTV:CAC ratio declined from 4.4x (2024) to 2.7x (2025), below sustainable 3.0x threshold')
evidence.source: Synthetic case design - SaaS metrics modeling

evidence.finding: Cohort-level churn acceleration (e.g., 'Year-1 churn rate for 2024 cohort: 18%. Year-1 churn rate for 2025 cohort: 28% (estimated at 6-month mark, projected to 35% at 12-month mark)')
evidence.source: Synthetic case design - cohort churn modeling

evidence.finding: CAC inflation (e.g., 'Blended CAC increased 40% from $32k (2024 average) to $45k (2025 average). Primary driver: cost-per-acquisition in core segment rising due to market saturation; secondary channel CAC much higher at $68k')
evidence.source: Synthetic case design - marketing CAC modeling

ownerConstraintProfile.budgetBand: MEDIUM (post-Series B, but constrained by capital efficiency requirements)
ownerConstraintProfile.staffCapacity: MEDIUM (dedicated finance/analytics team, but founders focused on fundraising and product)
